title: External Adapter Evaluability Contract and Certification
author: Priya Nair
body:
Overview:
This page defines the evaluability contract, minimum test matrix, and certification workflow for external model adapters and third-party model bundles that Redwood Inference may host or enable via Dedicated/Private deployments. The goal is to ensure adapters are predictable, testable, and safe to run through our eval harness, quantization profile tooling, and production-facing regression triage pipelines.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to any external adapter, model wrapper, or conversion artifact submitted by partners or third-party vendors for use in Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private modes.
- Covers behavior-level evaluation (quality), perf-level evaluation (latency/throughput), and operational evaluation (memory, KV cache correctness, failure modes).
- Does not replace product-specific acceptance criteria (service owners may add stricter domain requirements).

Why a contract matters:
1. Third-party adapters often introduce opaque preprocessing, tokenization mismatches, or kernel incompatibilities that create subtle quality regressions after quantization or at different sequence lengths.
2. A repeatable contract enables automated certification in our CI, preventing onboarding regressions and shortening review cycles.
3. It provides clear triage playbooks when regressions surface in production.

Definitions:
- Adapter: a packaging layer that converts a published model checkpoint into Redwood-serving artifacts (tokenizer, model config, conversion metadata).
- Evaluability: the property that an adapter exposes deterministic inputs/outputs for the eval harness and provides telemetry hooks required by Redwood tooling.
- Certification: successful completion of all gates in the test matrix and signoff by the model onboarding owner.

Ownership and roles:
- Partner / Vendor: provides adapter artifacts, conversion notes, and a minimal test manifest.
- Model Onboarding Team: gatekeeper for certification, coordinates evaluations and manual review.
- Eval Platform / CI Owners: run automated harness, collect telemetry, and provide artifacts for SRE and Quantization teams.
- Security & Compliance: reviews any restricted data handling or KMS/HSM interactions.

Certification gates (must pass all):
1) Sanity and determinism gate
   - Run the canonical smoke-suite (100 deterministic prompts).
   - Requirement: 100% successful runs (no crashes), response latency within baseline bounds (<= 2x reference unconstrained), and deterministic tokenization for identical inputs.

2) Tokenization & detokenization fidelity
   - Verify round-trip detokenization across a representative set of multilingual and edge-case tokens (control list provided by eval team).
   - Requirement: character-level equivalence for canonical examples; documented divergences permitted only if annotated in adapter manifest.

3) Eval harness integration gate
   - Adapter must expose an evaluation manifest (see example below) readable by the eval harness.
   - Must pass the functional evals: intent-preservation, hallucination-control, and slot-filling where applicable.

4) Quantization compatibility gate
   - Run quantized inference profiles (8-bit, 4-bit configurations supported by runtime).
   - Metrics: semantic-similarity delta <= configured QoQ threshold (default: 0.06 embedding cosine drop or 3% generation quality delta on chosen metric); memory and peak GPU allocations within expected budget.

5) Performance & throughput gate
   - 95th percentile token latency and median throughput tests across short (16 tokens), medium (256 tokens), and long (2048 tokens) contexts.
   - Requirement: 95th-pct latency within SLO for targeted deployment class (hosted/dedicated/private). See table below.

6) Stability and failure-mode gate
   - Injected fault tests: OOM, corrupted KV cache, network flakiness, and abrupt process restart.
   - Requirement: adapter should fail gracefully, return structured errors, and not corrupt shared caches. Recovery path documented.

7) Telemetry & observability gate
   - Adapter must emit adapter_id, model_version, tokenizer_version, quant_profile_id, and deterministic request hash in traces/metrics.
   - Must provide mapping to Redwood standard metric names: redwood.adapter.version, redwood.eval.loss_estimate, redwood.quant.status.

Certification test matrix (summary table):
| Gate | Example tests | Pass criterion | Owner |
|------|---------------|----------------|-------|
| Sanity | smoke-suite (100 prompts) | no crash, tokenization deterministic | Partner / Eval CI |
| Tokenization | round-trip tests for 24 languages | character equivalence or documented note | Partner / Onboarding |
| Functional eval | intent-preservation, factuality probes | PASS on primary slice set (>= 90% of probes) | Eval Team |
| Quantization | 8-bit/4-bit replay tests | semantic delta <= 0.06 | Quant Team |
| Perf | 16/256/2048 token runs | latency SLOs (see SLO table) | Perf Bench |
| Stability | OOM and restart tests | clean failure + documented recovery | SRE / Onboarding |

SLO reference (deployment class targets):
- Hosted API (free/standard tiers): median token latency < 40ms (short context), 95th < 225ms; throughput targets vary with plan.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU): median token latency < 25ms (short context), 95th < 150ms.
- Private on-prem (customer-configurable): target baseline provided during onboarding; certification verifies against declared baseline.

Promotion and release workflow (high level):
1. Partner submits adapter bundle + manifest to the onboarding repo and opens an onboarding request ticket.
2. Eval CI automatically schedules: smoke-suite, tokenization checks, and functional evals on sample probes.
3. Quant team runs parallel quant compatibility sweep; perf bench runs on matching hardware sizing.
4. If all gates pass: Onboarding owner creates a candidate release and tags for shadow experiments.
5. Shadow canary: run production-weighted shadow for 72 hours on non-critical traffic or replayed workload.
6. Monitoring window: evaluate response stability index (RSI) and telemetry adherence.
7. Final signoff: onboarding owner + SRE + Quantization lead.

Automated CI recipe (examples):
- Example adapter manifest (YAML snippet to include in bundle):
  ---
  adapter_id: "vendor-x/adapter-bert-slim-v1"
  model_family: "bert-qa"
  tokenizer: "sentencepiece-v2"
  supported_quant_profiles: ["int8-default","q4f_fast"]
  smoke_suite_hash: "sha256:..."
  test_seed_list: ["seed-a","seed-b"]

- CI job names and brief behavior:
  - adapter-smoke: runs smoke-suite and tokenization checks; exit non-zero on mismatch.
  - adapter-functional: runs eval harness scenarios and produces a JSON artifact with metrics.
  - adapter-quant-sweep: compiles quantized artifact variants and runs replayed probes.
  - adapter-perf-bench: runs block-throughput runs on target hardware and uploads trace files.

Telemetry contract (fields and semantics):
- redwood.adapter.id: stable string identifier for the adapter (immutable per release).
- redwood.adapter.artifact_hash: SHA256 of the packaged artifact (used in reproducibility).
- redwood.quant.profile: quantization profile id used for inference.
- redwood.evaluator.manifest_version: manifest schema version that was used to orchestrate the evaluation.
- request.eval_request_hash: deterministic hash for the request payload used in the harness.

Regression triage and rollback playbook (short):
1. If production detects a rise in regression alerts tied to adapter_id, immediately trigger the adapter-failure playbook.
2. Snapshot failing request hashes and surface them to the model-oncall queue.
3. Run binary-bisect using archived artifacts and replay against the quantized artifact variants to isolate commit/quant-change.
4. If root cause is adapter change, rollback to the previous certified adapter artifact and open an RCA.

Onboarding checklist (must be included in the PR):
- adapter bundle (weights, tokenizer, conversion notes)
- adapter manifest (schema v2)
- smoke-suite seed file and expected artifacts
- minimal functional probe set and expected metrics
- declared quant profiles and memory budgets
- documented recovery steps for OOM or cache corruption

Failure modes and escalation notes:
- Non-deterministic tokenization: reject the bundle until tokenization library is stabilized or adapter provides mapping tables.
- Excessive semantic drift after quantization: mark as conditional-pass with enforced shadowing for 14 days and higher telemetry sampling.
- Telemetry omissions: certification blocked until required fields emitted.

Example commands and artifacts for reviewers:
- Run smoke suite locally (dockerized):
  docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/work redwood/eval-runner:stable 
    --adapter /work/adapter-bundle.tar.gz --smoke-seed /work/smoke-seed.json 

- Generate evaluation manifest (local helper):
  rwd-evalgen manifest create --adapter-id vendor-x/adapter-bert-slim-v1 --probes probes/primary.json --out manifest.yaml

Appendix A: Minimal manifest schema (human-readable)
- manifest_version: v2
- adapter_id: string
- model_family: string
- tokenizer: string
- quant_profiles: list[string]
- smoke_suite_hash: string
- probes: list["path/to/probe.json"]

Appendix B: Common triage templates
- Incident title: "Adapter regression: {adapter_id} semantic delta spike"
- Initial triage checklist:
  1) Confirm adapter_id and artifact_hash.
  2) Run adapter-smoke locally and attach logs.
  3) Run quant replay for reported probe hashes.
